newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares fall on crown turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares fall on crown turmoil.

text.p: Czech shares closed lower on Friday, hit by investor nervousness after another day of intense pressure on the Czech crown.
Dealers said the money market would continue to influence stock prices when the markets reopened on Monday.
"I would expect the money markets would be very busy again on Monday and so it will depend on what happens with the rates and the Czech crown," said Zivnostenska banka dealer Ivan Kusacek.
The PX50 index closed 1.05 percent lower at 509.2.
"Especially this morning, prices dropped and then blue chips recovered a bit. The afternoon was not so hectic," said Kusacek.
He said selling was mainly by domestic investors with foreigners waiting on the sidelines.
Komercni Banka fell 57 crowns to 1,938, SPT Telecom slipped five crowns to 3,230 and power utility CEZ closed seven lower at 948 crowns.
Wood and Company trader Jiri Zelinka said volumes had been low and he said a further easing in the market was possible on Monday.
"It will stay in this position or possibly continue a bit lower," he said.
